disclosures.name: TestNonEscapingMap
disclosures.reason: structural: want-zero AllocsPerRun asserts over four shapes of a map that does not escape (a literal, `make` with no hint, with the constant hint 8, with a variable hint), each followed by `m[0] = 0`. Two independent causes each keep it red. R1 (load-bearing, R's sizing on windows at Release TC0, same built test binary re-run with one environment variable changed per arm): at TC0 the JIT drops Go-kept frames through inlining AND through implicit tail calls, so the child's runtime.Callers keeps 3 of Go's 12 frames (child7, func1, goexit); default tiering keeps all 12, and TC0 with DOTNET_JitNoInline=1 keeps exactly the frames whose call is not in tail position. Which frames exist in optimized CLR code is the JIT's decision, so no scoped marking can restore them, and this is a diagnostic-only crash-traceback assertion (the owner's 2026-09-28 principle). R2 (independent, R's sizing): caller PC tokens are interned per process in first-sight order, so the same binary gives the same frame a different token in the child and in the parent, and the parent cannot symbolize the child's PCs: a child PC names another frame or none. Its retirement direction, per-binary DETERMINISTIC caller tokens keyed on the assembly's position-map records, is queued as a caller-band design item and is not dispatched.
